updates.title: Claude Code Self-Hosted Environments Now in Public Beta
updates.summary: Anthropic launched self-hosted environments for Claude Code in public beta, letting teams on Team and Enterprise plans run Claude Code web, mobile, and desktop sessions on their own machines or containers via the new `claude self-hosted-runner` command. Sessions execute inside the organization's own network—adjacent to internal services, toolchains, and security controls—rather than on Anthropic's infrastructure. The feature is off by default and targets organizations whose network, compliance, or tooling requirements demand agent execution on infrastructure they control.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed directly from the official Claude Code changelog at code.claude.com and corroborated by multiple third-party coverage (Unite.AI, Artiverse, beri.net). Feature details (command name, plan requirements, default-off behavior) are consistent across sources. No red flags.

updates.title: Anthropic Ships Four Managed Agents API Upgrades: Session Budgets, Advisor Models, Geo Control, and GitHub Skills
updates.summary: Anthropic's August 7 platform release notes detail four significant additions to Claude Managed Agents. Developers can now set a hard spend budget on a session (pausing with a 'budget_reached' stop reason when hit), assign an 'advisor' model that the primary agent can consult mid-turn for strategic guidance, control which geographic region model inference runs in for data-residency requirements, and automatically load skills from a mounted GitHub repository's `.claude/skills` directory at session start.

updates.title: Claude Code Gives Me Very Few Models to Work With, and That's Exactly Why I Keep Going Back to It
updates.published_date: 2026-08-07 (approximate — confirmed early August 2026; exact date unverifiable due to site access restrictions)
updates.summary: XDA Developers published an opinion piece arguing that Claude Code's deliberately small, curated model roster is a feature rather than a limitation. The piece also notes Anthropic's enterprise escape hatches (the `availableModels` admin policy) for organizations that need to restrict which models developers can access.
